identity.name: JNK INDIA LIMITED
identity.industry: Refining & Petrochemical Process Equipment / Energy Transition

summary.oneLiner: JNK India delivered a blowout Q3 with revenue doubling YoY and EBITDA tripling, driven by strong execution in refining verticals and a shift to input-based accounting, while securing a robust pipeline including a potential $140M+ Dangote repeat opportunity and early traction from its Green Hydrogen JV.

one-line thesis: JNK India delivered a blowout Q3 with revenue doubling YoY and EBITDA tripling, driven by strong execution in refining verticals and a shift to input-based accounting, while securing a robust pipeline including a potential $140M+ Dangote repeat opportunity and early traction from its Green Hydrogen JV.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Rs 2,062 Mn (+112.8% YoY); EBITDA: Rs 295 Mn (+202.8% YoY, 14.3% margin); PAT: Rs 180 Mn (+534.1% YoY, 8.7% margin); Order Book: ~Rs 1,700 Cr (as of Jan 1); Net Debt: Not explicitly stated, but working capital limits utilized (Rs 470 Cr non-fund, Rs 70 Cr fund); One-offs: Rs 9.26 Mn charge for new labor code impact recognized in Q3.
guidance: Revenue Growth: ~40% for FY26 (maintained); Margin: 13-14% EBITDA (maintained despite labor code hit); Order Inflow: Expect Rs 400-600 Cr from BPCL Bina in next 2 quarters; Rs 200-250 Cr each from Middle East waste gas and domestic clean fuel projects in ~1 quarter; Capex/Commissioning: JV pilot projects taking off soon.
order book & pipeline: Total ~Rs 1,700 Cr (Jan 1); Includes Rs 1,050 Cr booked from BPCL Bina (of larger contract), with Rs 400-600 Cr pending over next 2 quarters; Chemdist JV order book ~Rs 100 Cr; Execution timeline avg 2-2.5 years.
segment / subsidiary detail: Fired Heaters: Core driver, major exposure to Dangote (Nigeria) and BPCL Bina; Flares/Incinerators: Driven by regulatory retrofit/compliance rather than greenfield; Green Hydrogen/Chemdist: Early stage, Rs 23 Cr revenue in Q3, targeting 10-15% of standalone revenue in 2-3 years; Biogas/CBG: Technology stabilization challenges, policy support via budget excise exemption.
growth verticals / optionality: Dangote Refinery expansion (doubling capacity) offers ~$140M fired heater opportunity + 4 reformer packages ($30-40M each); Qualification for large cracking furnace contracts opens door to bigger petchem projects; JV with Chemdist provides IP-led growth in green hydrogen/CCUS; Middle East export pipeline (Rs 200-250 Cr imminent).
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin 14.3% (vs guided 13-14%); Pressure from Rs 9.26 Mn labor code charge; Accounting shift from output to input method normalized margins after legacy project drag; Material cost 74% (down from 78%), expected range 70-75% depending on service mix.
capex / expansion: No major standalone capex mentioned; Fabrication capacity (Mundra) currently underutilized due to lack of export execution, not a bottleneck as model relies on customer-approved shops near sites; Focus on R&D and pilot projects for Green Hydrogen/CBG via JV.
capital allocation: Working capital limits sufficient (Rs 500 Cr non-fund, Rs 100 Cr fund); Bank guarantee burden eased via JNK Global partnership for large contracts (e.g., BPCL); Performance guarantees (10% of contract value) will remain blocked post-project completion.
risks & watch-items: Execution timing slippage (Reliance spilling to Q1 FY27); Dangote order finalization uncertainty (expected Q3 FY27); CBG technology/feedstock stabilization issues limiting domestic uptake; Dependency on large lump-sum orders causing quarterly volatility; Labor code compliance costs.
management quality / tone: Confident and optimistic; Emphasizes strong order book, strategic positioning in energy transition, and successful JV ramp-up; Acknowledges near-term margin pressure from one-offs but reaffirms guidance; Cautious on CBG timeline due to tech hurdles.
non-obvious takeaways: Accounting policy shift (output to input method) is the primary driver of margin normalization, not operating leverage or pricing; Mundra facility utilization is low not due to demand but lack of specific export projects under execution; JV revenue (Rs 23 Cr) already flowing in first quarter of operation, faster than typical R&D spin-offs; Bank guarantee structure via JNK Global significantly de-risks balance sheet for large tenders.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Need for high-efficiency fired heaters and reformers in refinery expansion | JNK India Limited | beneficiary | High | Direct beneficiary of Dangote Refinery expansion ($140M+ opportunity) and BPCL Bina execution; unique qualification for large cracking furnaces. |
| Technology stabilization and feedstock issues in CBG sector | Pure-play CBG developers | loser | Med | Sector facing delays due to tech/feedstock hurdles, though JNK is positioned to benefit once solutions stabilize via European partnerships. |
| Scaling green hydrogen production under National Mission | Chemdist Group (Unlisted JV Partner) | beneficiary | High | JV with JNK provides commercial pathway for Chemdist's IP in green hydrogen/CCUS, leveraging JNK's execution muscle. |
